.. _arduino_heartrate:

======================
1.4 Heart Rate Sensor
======================

Reading pulse data from the MAX30102 heart rate and pulse oximeter sensor via I2C.

Overview
========

This project demonstrates how to interface with a biomedical sensor. The MAX30102 uses an IR LED and photodetector to measure blood volume changes in your fingertip, which are processed to calculate your heart rate (BPM).

What You'll Learn
=================

* Using third-party sensor libraries (SparkFun MAX3010x)
* Processing real-time sensor data
* Simple beat-detection and BPM calculation algorithms

Pin Connections
===============

========== ========
MAX30102   ESP32-S3
========== ========
SDA        GPIO 2
SCL        GPIO 1
VCC        3.3V
GND        GND
========== ========

How the Code Works
==================

The sketch initializes the MAX30105 sensor with its default settings and continuously reads IR samples:

.. code-block:: cpp

   MAX30105 particleSensor;
   particleSensor.begin();
   particleSensor.setup();

   long irValue = particleSensor.getIR();

A finger-detection algorithm with hysteresis (8-sample window, adjustable thresholds) determines if a finger is placed on the sensor. Beat detection identifies each pulse, and a rolling average (8-beat window) calculates BPM. Unreasonable values (<45 or >180 BPM) are rejected.

.. code-block:: cpp

   if (checkForBeat(irValue)) {
       float bpm = 60000.0 / (millis() - lastBeat);
       // Add to rolling average
   }

Expected Result
===============

Place your fingertip gently on the MAX30102 sensor. The Serial Monitor (115200 baud) will display::

   BPM: 72  IR: 85200
   BPM: 73  IR: 86100

.. note::
   Keep your finger still for accurate readings. It may take a few seconds for the BPM value to stabilize.
